state.heading: Three Jevs, three primitives, one call
state.text: Plate II. — The words — in which one call carries many questions and code does the rest folio ii Three Jevs, three primitives, one call After this plate you can read any pack in the catalog, tell a legal question from one that belongs in code, and describe what actually crosses the wire. There are three things called Jev , and they must never be fused. A vendor model that answers typed questions in a few hundred milliseconds. A kernel that decides what may compose. A closed runtime for work items. Everything else in these repos is a way of asking the first one a question and letting code act on the answer. TypeSafe Jev is the model, pinned at jev-1.13.0 . It does not chat. You send one state and a set of named questions; it returns one typed answer per question with a probability. Three primitives cover everything: Noul , the probability that a yes/no is true; Choice , a closed set of keys with a distribution over them; Score , an ordered rubric of two to ten levels. The gateway spells Noul as boolean ; the native API does not. manutej/jev is the kernel: five colours for ports, an operad that composes only on a colour match, and a score that turns a distribution into GREEN, AMBER or RED. Digest Rust JEV is the work runtime: nine kinds of item, four ways to clarify one, ten commands, nothing else. The word that matters most is pack : a set of literal questions about one record, plus the list of judgements deliberately handed to code, called notForJev . Build a request below fr …

state.heading: Fifteen laws that every repo keeps
state.text: Plate III. — The laws — in which fifteen rules are found in more than one repo folio iii Fifteen laws that every repo keeps After this plate you can name the rule behind any screen decision, cite where it is written, and say what breaks when it is bent. A law here is not a preference. It is a rule stated independently by at least two repos that never met, which is the closest thing this ecosystem has to a measurement of its own doctrine. The collector already pins eighteen contracts, C0 to C17. The fifteen laws below are what you get when you read the lab's thirty-five properties, the tape's specs, the secretary's hard rules and the kernel's invariants side by side and keep only what repeats. Each law carries a screen rule, because a law that a page cannot show is a law nobody will keep. Pick a law. The card shows the rule in the voice a button would use, the repos that state it, the contract it maps to, and the scenarios in Plate VII that pass through it. A rail is a contract an agent may not leave. Rails are not suggestions. jev-elder · RAILS.md Fail closed. Compose only on GREEN. manutej/jev · README.md Quote or drop. state.heading: One gate , three dialects
state.text: Plate IV. — The gate — in which one verdict is spoken in three dialects folio iv One gate , three dialects After this plate you can take any answer with its probability and say whether code may act, a person must look, or nothing continues, in each repo's words. Four repos built the same gate and gave it four names. The kernel says GREEN, AMBER, RED . The bench says ACT, REVIEW, HOLD. The kit says true, false, escalate. The tape and the depth-4 schema say compose, escalate, refuse. Move the slider and watch all of them answer at once. The numbers are the repos' own. The bench acts on a Noul at p ≤ 0.15 or p ≥ 0.85 and on a Choice when its entropy is under 0.15 ( bench/README.md ). The tape's client calls 0.4 to 0.6 the mid band and escalates it ( src/typesafe/contract.ts ). The kernel ships a fill only when allowed mass is at least 0.72 and toxin mass at most 0.12; toxin above 0.12 or allowed under 0.40 is RED ( score.ts ). A Score acts when the weighted value sits within 0.15 of a level ( confidence.ts ). Between the ends and the mid band there is a stretch where the dialects disagree. That stretch is where a shared decide() would live; the Hub lists it as the first engine gate to strike. Gate on entropy, not confidence. JEV-works · README.md Mid-band ~0.5 is a coin flip. Escalate. jev-elder · rails/CONTRACTS.md, C2 Agreement is not correctness. jev-elder · README.md Hand of the maker: the noise band is 0.11 overall, about 0.07 for booleans and scores and 0.15 for choices. state.heading: Four arms and nothing else
state.text: Plate V. — The arms — in which a closed sum refuses politely folio v Four arms and nothing else After this plate you can capture a line, clarify it into exactly one typed item or leave it where θ says, and explain why the runtime refuses a fifth kind. The Digest runtime is small on purpose. An Inbox line holds text and a timestamp . Clarify moves it into one of four arms, or leaves it. Nothing has a due date, a tag or a priority, and the reason is not austerity: every field you do not have is a field nobody can misuse. The one model call in this plate is a Choice with four keys: NextAction, Project, Someday, Waiting. Below a threshold the line stays in the Inbox for a person. The recipe insists the threshold has two names, confidence_theta owned by Composition and top_prob_floor owned by policy, both 0.60 as a trial. Move them separately and the difference stops being abstract. The distributions on the lines below are fixtures, on the sample tint, so you can feel the instrument without a key. Then try the buttons that a normal task app would offer. Each one is refused by the type, with the reason from the source. Do not fuse with manutej/jev jev-kernel. jev-domain · README.md uncertain is not a criterion. jev-elder · meta/CLARIFY-CHOICE-RECIPE.md Hand of the maker: the box copy of SPEC-v0 lists eight arms. The frozen Block B handoff allows four. The runtime code has four. The eight is a residual, recorded, not resolved. The instrument · clarify a line confidence_theta · Compo …

state.heading: Where the bricks sit
state.text: Plate VI. — The bricks — in which every file is set on its shelf folio vi Where the bricks sit After this plate you can name the five shelves, place any block on one, and say which engine it feeds and whether it is real, half-built, or promised. Five shelves. Contracts at the bottom, then the services as they are, then five engines assembled from them, then the tools and workers that wrap an engine for a person or a schedule, then the platforms where people live. A brick's colour is its constellation; its edge says whether it exists. An engine is a name for code that already exists in more than one place and agrees. The Gate Engine is Plate IV. The Clarify Engine is Plate V. The Question Engine is the lab's lint, measure and catalog. The Tape Engine is four ledger schemas with no shared writer. The Collector Engine is the digest and the scripts that made this book. Choose an engine and the shelves keep only its bricks. Choose a status and see how much of an engine is promise. Four layers. Two effects. manutej/jev · README.md Does not swallow source repos. jev-elder · README.md TypeSafe qualifies. Code gates. Temporal records. jev-tape · README.md The instrument · choose an engine and a status The proof the engine, assembled When this is the wrong tool An engine is a name, not a binary. Naming five of them does not join their parts; it says where a join would go. The honest reading of this plate is a bill of materials: what is on the shelf, what is on order, and what the catal …

state.heading: Which piece answers which question
state.text: Plate VII. — The questions — in which each piece is asked what it is for folio vii Which piece answers which question After this plate you can take a question someone asks in a working day, walk the exact files that answer it, and say whether it runs today, needs one thing, or waits on a missing block. A scenario is a question a person actually asks. Its route is the ordered set of blocks that answer it , each with a role: sensor, pack, model, gate, recombine, actuator, ledger, human. The route is drawn only from files that exist; where a file is missing the hop is dashed and the scenario is gated. Twenty-one scenarios cover the business day, the developer's day and the agent's session. Six have been measured, with numbers in the repos. Eight run today given a key. Five are partial. Two wait on a missing block, and each says which. Choose who you are, then a question. Step through the route one hop at a time, or show it whole. Click any hop to see every other question that same block answers; that reverse index is how you learn which bricks are load-bearing. The question you ask is the product. The kernel's generated bank is counted by its templates, twenty per kind, not its sixteen hundred instances. Beside each pack is the count of judgements it hands to code: the notForJev list, which the lab calls the most valuable part of a set. questions are nearly free, state is the scarce resource JEV-works · question-bank/bank.ts …the most valuable part of each set JEV-works · question-bank/README.md, on notForJev The instrument · filter and sort noul choice score mlm restriction The proof the measured five When this is the wrong tool A count of questions is not a count of decisive questions. The lab's label-free measure finds two defects a count hides: questions that never leave the mid band and belong in code, and questions answered before they are asked. state.heading: Stakes and the assay
state.text: Plate IX. — The assay — in which every stake carries a stamp and every gate names its measurement folio ix Stakes and the assay After this plate you can tell what has been measured from what has been drawn, and read a stamp without needing its colour. The stamps are the honesty apparatus. ⚖ measured means a run in a repo produced a number. ✓ runnable means the files exist and want a key. ± partial means a hop is half-built. ⊘ gate means a load-bearing block is missing, and the row says what would strike it. Every stamp is a glyph with a word, so it survives grayscale and a screen reader. Below are the twenty-one scenarios and the fourteen designed experiences from the Hub, on one ledger. Filter by stamp to see the shape of the week: how much of this ecosystem is doctrine, how much is drawing, how much is number. Leads qualified: old question set, regex wins (92.2% vs 67.8%, McNemar 6 vs 152) JEV-works · NETER.md, §6 Not a live TypeSafe qualifier. No API keys. jev-tape-wiki · README.md The instrument · filter by stamp The proof what has a number When this is the wrong tool Measured on fixtures, on synthetic leads, or on public datasets is not measured in your inbox. The stamp says a number exists and where; it does not transfer the number to a new domain. That transfer is Q0 to Q9 in the lab's qualification protocol, run again. Where this goes hub/insights/INSIGHTS.md JEV-works · NETER.md jev-elder · EVAL-HARDEN.md ← Plate VIII. The catalog folio ix Plate X. The yield →

state.heading: The yield : what to build Monday
state.text: Plate X. — The yield — in which the order of work is the argument folio x The yield : what to build Monday After this plate you can name the next eight steps in order, and for each one say which questions from Plate VII it unlocks. The steps are ordered by how many questions each one turns from gated or partial to runnable. The first two take a week and unlock the whole business inbox. Nothing on this list is new development inside a source repo; each step strikes a gate that a repo already named. Pick a horizon. The steps outside it dim; the questions that become runnable inside it light. The count in the black panel is the yield. A model proposes, a person decides, truth scores both. Daylight Ledger · README "Zero hallucinations" means schema-bound output, not a correct classification. jev-playground · README.md The instrument · choose a horizon The proof the honest ledger When this is the wrong tool An order of work is a bet on yield, and yield here was computed from a drawing of routes, not from users. If the first hundred jev_log rows show the mid band is a third of the inbox rather than a tenth, the review queue outranks everything else on this list and the order changes. Rebuild the book after the first measure; the script that made it takes seconds. Where this goes The JEV Hub hub/VISION.md hub/handoff/ ← Plate IX. The assay folio x colophon →

state.heading: Type
state.text: Type Fraunces for the titles, ledes and marginalia, one italic noun per plate. Archivo for every word of interface, as Daylight Ledger prescribes. IBM Plex Mono for identifiers, paths and stamps, and for nothing else. Colour Daylight Ledger grounds and inks in both themes. Lamps go, hold, stop and pending keep their meaning and are never reused as decoration. Each constellation has one accent; each plate takes one of them. Sources Every quotation is verbatim from a file in the repos as read on 2026-09-24. Every number is from a file: hub/questions/catalog.json , hub/model/*.json , or the repo text it cites. Where no number exists the stamp says so. Technical note One file, no build, no keys, no calls to TypeSafe. Generated from hub/notebook/src.html and the model files by hub/scripts/collect-questions.mjs . Rebuild after any change to the repos.

Lamps go, hold, stop and pending keep their meaning and are never reused as decoration. Each constellation has one accent; each plate takes one of them. Sources Every quotation is verbatim from a file in the repos as read on 2026-09-24. Every number is from a file: hub/questions/catalog.json , hub/model/*.json , or the repo text it cites. Where no number exists the stamp says so. Technical note One file, no build, no keys, no calls to TypeSafe. Generated from hub/notebook/src.html and the model files by hub/scripts/collect-questions.mjs . Rebuild after any change to the repos.
